findings.issue: isBuildRender keys off the undocumented internal 'gracile-static' hostname the Gracile engine uses when rendering routes during vite build; it matches engine 0.12.0's render.ts today but is not a public API and could silently change on upgrade, re-introducing build-time API fetches that the spec forbids.
findings.suggestion: Keep the guard but add a version-pin comment and a build-time smoke check (e.g. fail the build if a handler fetches during the build render), or request an official flag from Gracile for build renders.

findings.issue: The Move API shape is declared twice, slightly differently, in the pokemon and moves routes.
findings.suggestion: Move the Move/MoveRow types into src/lib/data.ts alongside TypeDetail and import them in both routes.

findings.issue: popstate listener is added in connectedCallback and never removed, and the debounce timer isn't cleared on disconnect.
findings.suggestion: Store the listener and clearTimeout in a disconnectedCallback (or use AbortController for all listeners) — a pattern worth having before any future client-side routing is added.

findings.issue: No timeout or retry on API fetches; a slow upstream stalls requests and occupies concurrency slots indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Use AbortSignal.timeout() (Node 24 supports it) inside load() so a stuck upstream fails fast and frees its slot.

findings.issue: replaceWith on the #results node itself — the element carrying aria-live is replaced rather than updated, which some screen readers won't announce.
findings.suggestion: Keep the live region stable and replace only its childNodes.

findings.issue: Inline onerror="this.style.visibility='hidden'" attribute for missing sprites.
findings.suggestion: Prefer a data-attribute plus a tiny client script (or the existing elements) so a future CSP without 'unsafe-inline' doesn't break sprite fallback.

findings.issue: The catch-all 404 route never sets responseInit.status, unlike the detail routes (e.g. pokemon/[name].ts:300), so unmatched URLs may return 200.
findings.suggestion: Add a handler setting responseInit.status = 404 for consistency with the detail routes and the spec's encouragement.

summary: A well-crafted, idiomatic Gracile app: route handlers, document templates, the Hono adapter, and progressive-enhancement custom elements all follow the framework's current documented APIs, and the lib layering (api/data/format/templates) has clean boundaries. The main merge blocker is the undocumented 'gracile-static' hostname sentinel the build guard relies on. Everything else is nits I'd clear in a single review round.
